subject: Pricing & context-length profiling — follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Patricia Gomez <pgomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & context-length profiling — follow-up from demo

Hi Jordan / Patricia —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — great discussion. Per our ask, I wanted to capture a quick post-call recap and the information we need to qualify pricing and plan a short POC. TL;DR: we need a short profile of your typical prompt/completion tokens and rough % of calls needing longer context (8k / 32k / 128k) so we can model unit economics and recommend the right model/quantization strategy.

Recap / asks:
- Product use case: knowledge retrieval + summarization for clinical notes (post-indexing retrieval, multi-doc summarization, and redaction).
- Primary SLOs: median latency < 1s for short queries, tail latency acceptable for long-context jobs; quality of long-form summarization must be preserved.
- Key qualification items we need from you:
  1) Avg prompt tokens per request (examples or sample payloads are great)
  2) Avg completion tokens per request
  3) Monthly token volume estimate (prompt + completion) or daily active requests and typical tokens/request
  4) % of requests that need 8k vs 32k vs 128k context windows
  5) Target/acceptable $ per 1M tokens (or monthly budget range) so we can map to Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and propose a usage band / reserved capacity plan

Helpful files attached: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (pricing bands), acme_context_profile.csv (example CSV template you can fill), sample_payloads.jsonl (small sample of inputs) — feel free to redact PHI.

A couple of notes on cost levers:
- Average tokens drive cost directly; completions usually dominate unit cost for summarization workloads.
- Caching/prefix KV can reduce repeated prompt costs for retrieval-heavy flows.
- If >10% of requests require 32k/128k we recommend model variants tuned for long context (and possibly a different pricing band).
- For pricing exercises we often model three scenarios: conservative (low growth), expected, and aggressive (high growth + retention).

Next steps / proposed M.A.P.
- Jordan: send a 1-week sample of logs or a quick fill of acme_context_profile.csv (estimates are fine).
- We’ll run a quick cost model and return a POC proposal (2-week POC with 100k–1M tokens/day test band).
- If the numbers look good, we recommend starting with a 3-month reserved capacity commit to secure pricing and runway.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the CSV — otherwise if you can drop the numbers by Friday that’s perfect.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, acme_context_profile.csv, sample_payloads.jsonl

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Patricia Gomez <pgomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & context-length profiling — follow-up from demo

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We pulled some quick numbers and a very rough profile below (happy to share sanitized logs). High level: this is a summarization-heavy flow so completions are >2x prompts in most cases.

Quick profile (rough estimates):
- Avg prompt tokens: ~1,200 tokens (many retrieval prompts are 600–2,000 depending on number of docs included)
- Avg completion tokens: ~3,500 tokens for long summarizations; for short QA flow completions are ~250 tokens
- Token split: we estimate about 20% of calls are short QA (prompt 400 / completion 250), ~60% are mid-length summarizations (prompt 900 / completion 1,200), ~20% are long multi-doc summaries (prompt 2,500 / completion 6,500)
- Context window needs: ~70% of requests fit under 8k, ~25% need 32k, ~5% need 128k (these are the long multi-doc summaries where we stitch 20+ notes)
- Monthly volume: currently ~12M requests/month across users; rough average tokens/month ~1.4B tokens (prompt + completion) today; seasonality expected 10–20% lift Q3
- Budget: current internal target for inference spend is $10k–$30k/month to start (we can scale if unit economics make sense). Given current volumes we’re sensitive to $/1M token pricing in the $5–$25 range (different teams track different numbers).

Let us know if you want sanitized sample logs — we can export a 7-day sample with headers and token counts.

Jordan
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Health
jordan.lee@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Patricia Gomez <pgomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & context-length profiling — follow-up from demo

Jordan —

This is perfect, thanks for the quick profile — very helpful. A few follow-ups / how we’ll model this for pricing:

1) Unit economics (ballpark):
- Using your ~1.4B tokens/mo today, and your budget band $10k–$30k/month, that maps to a target blended $/1M tokens of roughly $7–$21. We’ll run detailed per-workload numbers, but thought that quick mapping was helpful.
- Completions skew heavily right here (your long summaries) and will drive most of cost. We recommend modeling separate bands for short QA vs long summaries.

2) Context-length recommendations:
- With ~30% of requests needing >8k, we recommend a mixed routing approach: route short/mid requests to a lower-cost 8k-optimized model and long jobs to a 32k/128k variant. That keeps unit costs predictable while preserving quality for long-form summarization.

3) Performance & cost levers we’ll propose in the POC:
- KV/prefix caching on retrieval hits to reduce prompt tokens by ~15–40% (where applicable)
- Batching and request shaping for lower-cost reserved capacity utilization
- Quantization/model-size trade-offs for long-context models if accuracy allows (we’ll benchmark)

4) POC proposal (two options):
A) Hosted POC — 2 weeks, 200M tokens total (sample-based), Redwood provides a temporary promotional pricing band and targeted engineering support to validate latency/quality.
B) Dedicated trial — 4 weeks, reserved node with burst capacity, we model your 1.4B/month run rate and recommend a 3-month reserved commit if you want predictable pricing.

Next steps: please share the 7-day sanitized sample logs (token counts + representative prompt/completion pairs) and we’ll return a cost model + recommended routing + POC pricing by EOD Monday. If you prefer, Rishi (cc’d) can schedule a short call to align on the POC scope this week.

Attached: I’ve included a short worked example (redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) showing per-1M token math for different model bands — will customize with your exact splits once we have logs.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, sample_proposal_summary.xlsx (stub)

Jordan
